```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
library(countdown)
library(patchwork)
library(moderndive)
library(gapminder)

# Colors from _brand.yml
clrs <- list(
  blue = "#2878B5",
  orange = "#E17C05",
  maroon = "#8A1538",
  purple = "#6F4C9B",
  green = "#2D934F",
  gray = "#696A6F"
)

theme_set(theme_grey(base_size = 14))
```

```{r}
#| label: make-data
#| include: false

# Toy data for drawing lines
cookies <- tibble(
  happiness = c(0.5, 2, 1, 2.5, 3, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 2, 3),
  cookies = 1:10
)

cookies_model <- lm(happiness ~ cookies, data = cookies)
cookies_b0 <- coef(cookies_model)[["(Intercept)"]]
cookies_b1 <- coef(cookies_model)[["cookies"]]

# ModernDive's UN data
UN_data_ch5 <- un_member_states_2024 |>
  select(
    country,
    life_exp = life_expectancy_2022,
    fert_rate = fertility_rate_2022
  ) |>
  na.omit()

demographics_model <- lm(fert_rate ~ life_exp, data = UN_data_ch5)
b0 <- coef(demographics_model)[["(Intercept)"]]
b1 <- coef(demographics_model)[["life_exp"]]

# Gapminder
gapminder_2007 <- gapminder |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  select(country, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap) |>
  mutate(gdp_1000 = gdpPercap / 1000)

continent_means <- gapminder_2007 |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(lifeExp), median = median(lifeExp))

lifeexp_model <- lm(lifeExp ~ continent, data = gapminder_2007)
lifeexp_points <- get_regression_points(lifeexp_model, ID = "country")

cont_b0 <- coef(lifeexp_model)[["(Intercept)"]]
cont_b <- coef(lifeexp_model)[-1] |>
  set_names(levels(gapminder_2007$continent)[-1])

# Example country for observed vs. fitted
afg <- lifeexp_points |> filter(country == "Afghanistan")

# Multiple regression
gdp_model <- lm(lifeExp ~ gdp_1000, data = gapminder_2007)
gdp_b1 <- coef(gdp_model)[["gdp_1000"]]

lifeexp_lots_model <- lm(lifeExp ~ gdp_1000 + continent, data = gapminder_2007)
mr_b0 <- coef(lifeexp_lots_model)[["(Intercept)"]]
mr_gdp <- coef(lifeexp_lots_model)[["gdp_1000"]]
mr_cont <- coef(lifeexp_lots_model)[-(1:2)] |>
  set_names(levels(gapminder_2007$continent)[-1])

# Offsets from Africa's line, staggered across the x-axis so the arrows don't overlap
mr_offsets <- tibble(
  continent = factor(names(mr_cont), levels = levels(gapminder_2007$continent)),
  offset = mr_cont,
  gdp_1000 = c(36, 12, 28, 44)
) |>
  mutate(
    africa = mr_b0 + mr_gdp * gdp_1000,
    lifeExp = africa + offset,
    label = paste0("+", round(offset, 2))
  )

# Two sliders and a bunch of switches
un_data <- un_member_states_2024 |>
  select(
    country,
    continent,
    life_exp = life_expectancy_2022,
    fert_rate = fertility_rate_2022,
    gdp_per_capita
  ) |>
  mutate(gdp_1000 = gdp_per_capita / 1000) |>
  drop_na(life_exp, fert_rate, gdp_1000)

un_model <- lm(life_exp ~ fert_rate + gdp_1000 + continent, data = un_data)
un_b <- coef(un_model)

# Hypothetical country for moving one slider (or switch) at a time
un_scenarios <- tribble(
  ~scenario,            ~fert_rate, ~gdp_1000, ~continent,
  "Start",              3,          10,        "Africa",
  "Fertility + 1",      4,          10,        "Africa",
  "GDP + $1,000",       3,          11,        "Africa",
  "Europe",             3,          10,        "Europe"
) |>
  mutate(life_exp_hat = predict(un_model, newdata = pick(everything())))

# Interpretation practice
# Predicted lines across one continuous x for each category of a group, holding
# all other continuous variables at their averages
model_lines <- function(model, x, group) {
  mf <- model.frame(model)
  held <- mf |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric) & !all_of(c(x, names(mf)[1])), mean))

  expand_grid(
    !!x := seq(min(mf[[x]]), max(mf[[x]]), length.out = 100),
    !!group := unique(mf[[group]])
  ) |>
    cross_join(held) |>
    mutate(.fitted = predict(model, newdata = pick(everything())))
}

schools_model <- lm(average_sat_math ~ perc_disadvan + size, data = MA_schools)
schools_b <- coef(schools_model)

evals_model <- lm(score ~ age + bty_avg + gender, data = evals)
evals_b <- coef(evals_model)

penguins_model <- lm(body_mass ~ flipper_len + bill_len + species, data = penguins)
penguins_b <- coef(penguins_model)

houses_model <- lm(price ~ living_area + age + fireplace, data = saratoga_houses)
houses_b <- coef(houses_model)
```

# Lines and regression<br>(review) {background-color="{{< brand color clr-7 >}}" background-image="/slides/img/background-hex-shapes.svg" background-opacity="0.25"}

## Models {.clr-7}

Models are simplified representations of complex things

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column .fragment}
![](img/Tyrannosaurus_Rex_Holotype.jpg){.shadow}
:::

::: {.column .fragment}
![](img/trexmodel.png){.shadow}
:::

::::

## Goal of regression {.clr-7}

[Use a model to explain (or predict) variation in an outcome using one or more explanatory variables]{.box-clr-7-light .large}

## Drawing lines with stats {.clr-7}

| $y = mx + b$ | | $\widehat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $y$ | Outcome variable (**Y**) | $\widehat{y}$ |
| $x$ | Explanatory variable (**X**) | $x$ | 
| $m$ | Slope | $b_1$ | 
| $b$ | y-intercept | $b_0$ | 

## Building models in R {.clr-7}

```{.r}
name_of_model <- lm(<Y> ~ <X>, data = <DATA>)
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="35%"}
::: {.fragment .small}
- `lm()` = **l**inear **m**odel
- `<Y> ~ <X>` is a **model formula** (same as in `get_correlation()`!)
:::
:::

::: {.column width="65%"}
::: {.fragment .small}
```{.r}
library(moderndive)

# Make the model
name_of_model <- lm(..., data = BLAH)

# Coefficients in a nice table
get_regression_table(name_of_model)

# Fitted values and residuals for 
# every observation
get_regression_points(name_of_model)
```
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-cookies-review
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: "100%"

ggplot(cookies, aes(x = cookies, y = happiness)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 10), ylim = c(0, 3)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10) +
  labs(x = "Cookies eaten", y = "Level of happiness") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = clrs$blue, se = FALSE)
```
:::

::: {.column .small width="40%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true

cookies_model <- lm(
  happiness ~ cookies,
  data = cookies
)
```
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%" .small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{happiness}} &= b_0 + b_1 \times \text{cookies} \\
\widehat{\text{happiness}} &= `r round(cookies_b0, 2)` + `r round(cookies_b1, 3)` \times \text{cookies}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.column .smaller width="40%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true

cookies_model |>
  get_regression_table() |>
  select(term, estimate)
```
:::

::::


## Templates (continuous X) {.clr-7}

::: {.small}
$$
\widehat{\text{happiness}} = b_0 + b_1 \times \text{cookies} \qquad
\widehat{\text{happiness}} = `r round(cookies_b0, 2)` + `r round(cookies_b1, 3)` \times \text{cookies}
$$
:::

::: {.list-table widths="1,0.5,3" .small}

- - Parameter
  - Term
  - Template

- - Intercept
  - $b_0$
  - Average value of **Y** when **X** is 0

- - Slope 
  - $b_1$
  - A one unit increase in **X** is *associated* with a $b_1$ increase (or decrease) in **Y**, on average

:::

::: {.list-table widths="0.5,4" .smaller .sp-before}

- - Parameter
  - Interpretation

- - Intercept
  - Average happiness is `r round(cookies_b0, 2)` for someone who eats 0 cookies

- - Slope 
  - On average, eating one more cookie is associated with a `r round(cookies_b1, 3)` increase in happiness

:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%" .small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{fert}\_\text{rate}} &= b_0 + b_1 \times \text{life}\_\text{exp} \\
\widehat{\text{fert}\_\text{rate}} &= `r round(b0, 2)` + (`r round(b1, 3)`) \times \text{life}\_\text{exp}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.column .smaller width="40%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true

demographics_model |>
  get_regression_table() |>
  select(term, estimate)
```
:::

::::


## Templates (continuous X) {.clr-7}

::: {.small}
$$
\widehat{\text{fert}\_\text{rate}} = b_0 + b_1 \times \text{life}\_\text{exp} \qquad
\widehat{\text{fert}\_\text{rate}} = `r round(b0, 2)` + (`r round(b1, 3)`) \times \text{life}\_\text{exp}
$$
:::

::: {.list-table widths="1,0.5,3" .small}

- - Parameter
  - Term
  - Template

- - Intercept
  - $b_0$
  - Average value of **Y** when **X** is 0

- - Slope 
  - $b_1$
  - A one unit increase in **X** is *associated* with a $b_1$ increase (or decrease) in **Y**, on average

:::

::: {.list-table widths="0.5,4" .smaller .sp-before}

- - Parameter
  - Interpretation

- - Intercept
  - In a country where life expectancy is 0 years, the average fertility rate would be `r round(b0, 2)`

- - Slope 
  - On average, a one-year increase in life expectancy is associated with a `r abs(round(b1, 3))` decrease in the fertility rate

:::

## Building the model {.clr-8}

::: {.smaller}
```{r}
#| echo: true
lifeexp_model <- lm(lifeExp ~ continent, data = gapminder_2007)
get_regression_table(lifeexp_model)
```
:::

::: {.fragment}
[Where'd Africa go?!]{.box-clr-8-light}
:::

## The base case {.clr-8}

[One category gets left out and<br>becomes the **base case**]{.box-clr-8 .medium}

::: {.fragment .small .sp-before}
Also called the baseline, reference category, or omitted category
:::

::: {.fragment}
R uses the first category (alphabetically, by default) as the base case, so here it's [Africa]{.text-clr-8}
:::

::: {.fragment}
[Every other coefficient is measured<br>relative to the base case]{.box-clr-8-light}
:::

## Translating results to math {.clr-8}

::: {.smaller}
```{r}
get_regression_table(lifeexp_model) |>
  select(term, estimate) |>
  tt() |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ b_0 + b_1 \times \text{Americas} + b_2 \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ b_3 \times \text{Europe} + b_4 \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ `r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` \times \text{Americas} + `r round(cont_b[["Asia"]], 2)` \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ `r round(cont_b[["Europe"]], 2)` \times \text{Europe} + `r round(cont_b[["Oceania"]], 2)` \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

## Switches {.clr-8}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%" .small}
```{r}
get_regression_table(lifeexp_model) |>
  select(term, estimate) |>
  tt() |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](img/switch-only.jpg){.shadow}
:::

::::

## Template for the intercept {.clr-8}

[$b_0$ is the average value of **Y**<br>for the base case]{.box-clr-8 .medium}

$$
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = `r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` \times \text{Americas} + \dots
$$

::: {.fragment}
[Average life expectancy in Africa is `r round(cont_b0, 2)` years]{.box-clr-8-light}
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
All switches are off, so this is just the average of the base case
:::

## Template for the other coefficients {.clr-8}

[On average, **Y** is $b$ higher (or lower) in this category, compared to the base case]{.box-clr-8 .medium}

$$
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = `r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` \times \text{Americas} + \dots
$$

::: {.fragment}
[On average, life expectancy in the Americas is `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` years higher than in Africa]{.box-clr-8-light}
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
It's **not** "a one unit increase in continent"!  
It's the offset from the base case
:::

## Flip the switches! {.clr-8}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%" .small}
| Switch on | $\widehat{\text{lifeExp}}$ |
|:---|:---|
| None (Africa) | $`r round(cont_b0, 2)`$ |
| Americas | $`r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` = `r round(cont_b0 + cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)`$ |
| Asia | $`r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Asia"]], 2)` = `r round(cont_b0 + cont_b[["Asia"]], 2)`$ |
| Europe | $`r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Europe"]], 2)` = `r round(cont_b0 + cont_b[["Europe"]], 2)`$ |
| Oceania | $`r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Oceania"]], 2)` = `r round(cont_b0 + cont_b[["Oceania"]], 2)`$ |
:::

::: {.column width="45%" .fragment}
::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true

gapminder |> 
  filter(year == 2007) |> 
  group_by(continent) |> 
  summarise(avg = mean(lifeExp))
```
:::

[These are just the averages for each continent!]{.box-clr-8-light .small}

:::

## Offsets from the base case {.clr-8}

```{r}
#| label: plot-gapminder-offsets
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: "100%"

continent_offsets <- continent_means |>
  filter(continent != "Africa") |>
  mutate(
    offset = mean - cont_b0,
    label = paste0("+", round(offset, 2))
  )

gapminder_means +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cont_b0, color = clrs$purple, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(
    data = continent_offsets,
    aes(x = continent, xend = continent, y = cont_b0, yend = mean),
    color = clrs$orange, linewidth = 1.25,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  geom_label(
    data = continent_offsets,
    aes(x = continent, y = (cont_b0 + mean) / 2, label = label),
    fontface = "bold", size = 4, color = clrs$orange
  ) +
  annotate(
    geom = "label", x = 1, y = cont_b0 - 6,
    label = paste0("Base case\n(intercept)\n", round(cont_b0, 2)),
    fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, color = clrs$purple
  )
```

## Observed vs. fitted values {.clr-8}

```{r}
#| label: plot-gapminder-afg
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "100%"

# Drop Afghanistan's jittered point so it only shows up once
(gapminder_means %+% filter(gapminder_2007, country != "Afghanistan")) +
  geom_segment(
    data = afg,
    aes(x = continent, xend = continent, y = lifeExp, yend = lifeExp_hat),
    color = clrs$orange, linewidth = 1.25,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), ends = "first", type = "closed")
  ) +
  geom_point(data = afg, aes(y = lifeExp), size = 4, color = clrs$maroon) +
  geom_point(data = afg, aes(y = lifeExp_hat), size = 4, shape = 15, color = clrs$maroon) +
  annotate(
    geom = "label", x = 3.25, y = afg$lifeExp,
    label = "Afghanistan", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5
  )
```

::: {.smaller}
[●]{.text-clr-2} **Observed value** ($y$): Afghanistan's actual life expectancy = `r round(afg$lifeExp, 2)`  
[■]{.text-clr-2} **Fitted value** ($\widehat{y}$): $`r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Asia"]], 2)` \times 1 = `r round(afg$lifeExp_hat, 2)`$ (the Asia average)  
[↓]{.text-clr-8} **Residual** ($y - \widehat{y}$): $`r round(afg$lifeExp, 2)` - `r round(afg$lifeExp_hat, 2)` = `r round(afg$residual, 2)`$
:::

## Residuals for every country {.clr-8}

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
get_regression_points(lifeexp_model, ID = "country")
```
:::

```{r}
lifeexp_points |>
  slice_head(n = 8) |>
  tt() |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.65) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

## Templates (categorical X) {.clr-8}

::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ `r round(cont_b0, 2)` + `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` \times \text{Americas} + `r round(cont_b[["Asia"]], 2)` \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ `r round(cont_b[["Europe"]], 2)` \times \text{Europe} + `r round(cont_b[["Oceania"]], 2)` \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.list-table widths="1,0.5,3" .small}

- - Parameter
  - Term
  - Template

- - Intercept
  - $b_0$
  - Average value of **Y** for the base case

- - Coefficient
  - $b_n$
  - On average, **Y** is $b_n$ higher (or lower) in this category, compared to the base case

:::

::: {.list-table widths="0.5,4" .smaller .sp-before}

- - Parameter
  - Interpretation

- - Intercept
  - Average life expectancy in Africa is `r round(cont_b0, 2)` years

- - Americas
  - On average, life expectancy in the Americas is `r round(cont_b[["Americas"]], 2)` years higher than in Africa

:::

## Sliders and switches {.clr-8}

![](img/slider-switch.jpg){.shadow width="80%" fig-align="center"}

:::: {.columns .small .box-center}

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Categorical **X**]{.box-clr-8 .large}

**Y** shifts by $b_n$<br>compared to the base case
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Continuous **X**]{.box-clr-7 .large}

**Y** changes by $b_n$
:::

# Multiple regression {background-color="{{< brand color clr-2 >}}" background-image="/slides/img/background-hex-shapes.svg" background-opacity="0.25"}

## Many explanations! {.clr-2}

```{r}
#| label: plot-gdp-continent
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.25
#| out-width: "100%"

plot_gdp <- ggplot(gapminder_2007, aes(x = gdp_1000, y = lifeExp)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = clrs$blue, se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "GDP per capita (thousands of $)", y = "Life expectancy (2007)")

plot_gdp + gapminder_means + plot_layout(axes = "collect")
```

Wealth *and* continent-level differences each explain some of the variation in life expectancy

## One at a time {.clr-2}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%" .smaller .fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: true

gdp_model <- lm(
  lifeExp ~ gdp_1000,
  data = gapminder_2007
)

gdp_model |>
  get_regression_table() |>
  select(term, estimate)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%" .smaller .fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: true

lifeexp_model <- lm(
  lifeExp ~ continent,
  data = gapminder_2007
)

lifeexp_model |>
  get_regression_table() |>
  select(term, estimate)
```
:::

::::

## Both at the same time {.clr-2}

[GDP per capita and continent both explain<br>*some* variation in life expectancy]{.box-clr-2}

::: {.small .incremental}
- On its own, a \$1,000 increase in GDP per capita is associated with a `r round(gdp_b1, 2)` year increase in life expectancy, on average
- On its own, life expectancy in Europe is `r round(cont_b[["Europe"]], 2)` years higher than in Africa, on average
:::

::: {.fragment}
[Some of that explanation is shared!]{.box-clr-2-light .medium}
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Richer countries are concentrated in some continents, so each variable is partly getting credit for the other
:::

## Building the model {.clr-2}

Add more explanatory variables with `+`

::: {.smaller}
```{r}
#| echo: true

lifeexp_lots_model <- lm(lifeExp ~ gdp_1000 + continent, data = gapminder_2007)
get_regression_table(lifeexp_lots_model)
```
:::

## Translating results to math {.clr-2}

::: {.smaller}
```{r}
get_regression_table(lifeexp_lots_model) |>
  select(term, estimate) |>
  tt() |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ b_0 + b_1 \times \text{GDP}_{1000} + b_2 \times \text{Americas} + b_3 \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ b_4 \times \text{Europe} + b_5 \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ `r round(mr_b0, 2)` + `r round(mr_gdp, 3)` \times \text{GDP}_{1000} + `r round(mr_cont[["Americas"]], 2)` \times \text{Americas} + `r round(mr_cont[["Asia"]], 2)` \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ `r round(mr_cont[["Europe"]], 2)` \times \text{Europe} + `r round(mr_cont[["Oceania"]], 2)` \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

## One line per continent {.clr-2}

```{r}
#| label: plot-parallel-slopes
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.25
#| out-width: "100%"

clrs_continent <- c(
  Africa = clrs$purple, Americas = clrs$orange, Asia = clrs$green,
  Europe = clrs$blue, Oceania = clrs$maroon
)

plot_parallel <- ggplot(gapminder_2007, aes(x = gdp_1000, y = lifeExp, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_parallel_slopes(se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.25) +
  scale_color_manual(values = clrs_continent) +
  labs(
    x = "GDP per capita (thousands of $)", y = "Life expectancy (2007)",
    color = NULL
  )

plot_parallel
```

::: {.smaller}
Same slope for GDP (`r round(mr_gdp, 3)`) in every continent; the continent switches shift the intercept
:::

## Switches shift the line {.clr-2}

```{r}
#| label: plot-parallel-shifts
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.25
#| out-width: "100%"

plot_parallel +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = mr_b0, slope = mr_gdp,
    color = clrs$purple, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = mr_offsets,
    aes(x = gdp_1000, xend = gdp_1000, y = africa, yend = lifeExp),
    linewidth = 1, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  geom_label(
    data = mr_offsets,
    aes(x = gdp_1000, y = (africa + lifeExp) / 2, label = label),
    fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  annotate(
    geom = "label", x = 47, y = mr_b0 + mr_gdp * 47 - 4,
    label = paste0("Base case: Africa\n(intercept = ", round(mr_b0, 2), ")"),
    fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, color = clrs$purple, hjust = 1
  )
```

::: {.smaller}
Each continent's coefficient is how far its line is shifted above (or below) Africa's line
:::

## {.clr-2 .center}

![](img/mixer-board.jpg){.shadow width="100%" fig-align="center"}

## Filtering out variation {.clr-2}

[Each **X** in the model explains<br>some portion of the variation in **Y**]{.box-clr-2 .medium}

::: {.fragment .small}
This will often change the simple regression coefficients
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
| | On its own | In the model with both |
|:---|:---:|:---:|
| GDP per capita (\$1,000s) | `r round(gdp_b1, 3)` | `r round(mr_gdp, 3)` |
| Europe | `r round(cont_b[["Europe"]], 2)` | `r round(mr_cont[["Europe"]], 2)` |
:::

::: {.fragment}
[Interpretation is trickier, since you can only ever move **one** slider or switch at a time]{.box-clr-2-light}
:::

## Templates (multiple X) {.clr-2}

::: {.small}
$$
\widehat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \times x_1 + b_2 \times x_2 + \dots + b_n \times x_n
$$
:::

::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ b_0 + b_1 \times \text{GDP}_{1000} + b_2 \times \text{Americas} + b_3 \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ b_4 \times \text{Europe} + b_5 \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.list-table widths="1,0.5,3" .smaller}

- - Parameter
  - Term
  - Template

- - Intercept
  - $b_0$
  - Average value of **Y** when all continuous **X**s are 0 and all categorical **X**s are the base case

- - Continuous
  - $b_n$
  - *Taking all other variables in the model into account*, a one unit increase in **X**~n~ is associated with a $b_n$ increase (or decrease) in **Y**, on average

- - Categorical
  - $b_n$
  - *Taking all other variables in the model into account*, **Y** is $b_n$ higher (or lower) in this category compared to the base case, on average

:::

## Templates (multiple X) {.clr-2}

::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{lifeExp}} = &\ `r round(mr_b0, 2)` + `r round(mr_gdp, 3)` \times \text{GDP}_{1000} + `r round(mr_cont[["Americas"]], 2)` \times \text{Americas} + `r round(mr_cont[["Asia"]], 2)` \times \text{Asia} \\
&+ `r round(mr_cont[["Europe"]], 2)` \times \text{Europe} + `r round(mr_cont[["Oceania"]], 2)` \times \text{Oceania}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.list-table widths="0.6,4" .small .sp-before}

- - Parameter
  - Interpretation

- - Intercept
  - In an African country with a GDP per capita of \$0, average life expectancy would be `r round(mr_b0, 2)` years

- - GDP
  - Controlling for continent, a \$1,000 increase in GDP per capita is associated with a `r round(mr_gdp, 2)` year increase in life expectancy, on average

- - Europe
  - Controlling for GDP per capita, life expectancy in Europe is `r round(mr_cont[["Europe"]], 2)` years higher than in Africa, on average

:::

## "Controlling for…" {.clr-2}

::: {.fragment}
[These all mean the same thing!]{.box-clr-2-light}
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Controlling for…
- Taking all other variables in the model into account…
- Holding … constant
- Accounting for…
- Adjusting for…
:::

::: {.fragment .sp-before-half .small}
We're (1) comparing countries that have the same values for every other variable in the model, or (2) filtering out the variation that comes from the other variables, or (3) and isolating just one slider or switch
:::

## Lots of correlations at once {.clr-2}

::: {.small}
`get_correlation()` only works with two variables at a time; `select()` a bunch of numeric columns and pipe them into `cor()` to get a **correlation matrix**
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="45%" .small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

un_data |>
  select(
    life_exp,
    fert_rate,
    gdp_1000
  ) |>
  cor()
```
:::

::: {.column width="55%" .small .fragment}
```{r}
un_data |>
  select(life_exp, fert_rate, gdp_1000) |>
  cor() |>
  round(2)
```
:::

::::

::: {.fragment .small}
How is **Y** related to each **X**, *and* how are the **X**s related to each other?
:::

::: {.fragment .smaller}
If any columns have missing values, add `use = "complete.obs"` (it's like `na.rm = TRUE`): `cor(use = "complete.obs")`
:::

## Lots of sliders and switches! {.clr-2}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%" .small}
```{r}
#| echo: true

un_model <- lm(
  life_exp ~ fert_rate +
    gdp_1000 + continent,
  data = un_data
)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.small}
- **Sliders**: fertility rate *and* GDP per capita
- **Switches**: continent (Africa is the base case)
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}

::: {.column .small}
```{.r}
un_model |> 
  get_regression_table() |> 
  select(term, estimate)
```
:::

::: {.column .small}

```{r}
un_model |> 
  get_regression_table() |> 
  select(term, estimate)
```
:::

::::

## Move one slider/switch at a time {.clr-2}

::: {.small}
Imagine an African country with a fertility rate of 3 and a GDP per capita of \$10,000
:::

```{r}
un_scenarios |>
  mutate(
    gdp_1000 = scales::label_dollar()(gdp_1000 * 1000),
    change = round(life_exp_hat - first(life_exp_hat), 3),
    life_exp_hat = round(life_exp_hat, 2)
  ) |>
  set_names(c("Scenario", "Fertility rate", "GDP per capita", "Continent", "Predicted life exp.", "Change")) |>
  tt() |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.7) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

::: {.fragment}
[You can only interpret one slider or switch at a time;<br>keep the others constant]{.box-clr-2-light}
:::

## Interpreting everything {.clr-2}

::: {.list-table widths="0.6,4" .small}

- - Parameter
  - Interpretation

- - Intercept
  - In an African country with a fertility rate of 0 and a GDP per capita of \$0, average life expectancy would be `r round(un_b[["(Intercept)"]], 2)` years (not a real country!)

- - Fertility
  - Taking GDP per capita and continent into account, a one-child increase in the fertility rate is associated with a `r abs(round(un_b[["fert_rate"]], 2))` year decrease in life expectancy, on average

- - GDP
  - Holding fertility and continent constant, a \$1,000 increase in GDP per capita is associated with a `r round(un_b[["gdp_1000"]], 3)` year increase in life expectancy, on average

- - Europe
  - Controlling for fertility and GDP per capita, life expectancy in Europe is `r round(un_b[["continentEurope"]], 2)` years higher than in Africa, on average

:::

## SAT scores in Massachusetts {.clr-3}

::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{SAT}\_\text{math}} =&\ `r round(schools_b[["(Intercept)"]], 2)` + (`r round(schools_b[["perc_disadvan"]], 2)`) \times \text{perc}\_\text{disadvan}\ + \\
& (`r round(schools_b[["sizemedium"]], 2)`) \times \text{medium} + (`r round(schools_b[["sizelarge"]], 2)`) \times \text{large}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

:::: {.columns}


## SAT scores in Massachusetts {.clr-3}

::: {.incremental .small}
- **Intercept**: A *small* school with 0% economically disadvantaged students would have an average math SAT score of `r round(schools_b[["(Intercept)"]], 2)`
- **% disadvantaged**: Controlling for school size, a one percentage point increase in economically disadvantaged students is associated with a `r abs(round(schools_b[["perc_disadvan"]], 2))` point decrease in average math SAT scores, on average
- **Medium**: Taking the % of disadvantaged students into account, medium schools score `r abs(round(schools_b[["sizemedium"]], 2))` points lower than small schools, on average
- **Large**: Taking the % of disadvantaged students into account, large schools score `r abs(round(schools_b[["sizelarge"]], 2))` points lower than small schools, on average
:::

## Teaching evaluations {.clr-3}

::: {.small}
$$
\widehat{\text{score}} = `r round(evals_b[["(Intercept)"]], 2)` + (`r round(evals_b[["age"]], 3)`) \times \text{age} + `r round(evals_b[["bty_avg"]], 3)` \times \text{bty}\_\text{avg} + `r round(evals_b[["gendermale"]], 3)` \times \text{male}
$$
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-practice-evals
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.25
#| out-width: "100%"

ggplot(evals, aes(x = bty_avg, y = score, color = gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(
    data = model_lines(evals_model, "bty_avg", "gender"),
    aes(y = .fitted),
    linewidth = 1.25
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(clrs$purple, clrs$green)) +
  labs(
    x = "Average beauty rating (1–10)",
    y = "Teaching evaluation score (1–5)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%" .smaller}
```{.r}
lm(score ~ age + bty_avg + gender,
   data = evals)
```

```{r}
get_regression_table(evals_model) |>
  select(term, estimate) |>
  tt() |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```
:::

::::

## Teaching evaluations {.clr-3}

::: {.incremental .small}
- **Intercept**: A 0-year-old female professor with a beauty rating of 0 would have an average evaluation score of `r round(evals_b[["(Intercept)"]], 2)` (not a real professor!)
- **Age**: Controlling for beauty and gender, a one-year increase in a professor's age is associated with a `r abs(round(evals_b[["age"]], 3))` point decrease in evaluation scores, on average
- **Beauty**: Holding age and gender constant, a one-point increase in beauty rating is associated with a `r round(evals_b[["bty_avg"]], 3)` point increase in evaluation scores, on average
- **Male**: Taking age and beauty into account, male professors have evaluation scores that are `r round(evals_b[["gendermale"]], 3)` points higher than female professors, on average
:::

## Penguin weights {.clr-3}

::: {.small}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\text{body}\_\text{mass}} = &\ (`r round(penguins_b[["(Intercept)"]], 1)`) + `r round(penguins_b[["flipper_len"]], 1)` \times \text{flipper}\_\text{len} + `r round(penguins_b[["bill_len"]], 1)` \times \text{bill}\_\text{len} \\
&+ (`r round(penguins_b[["speciesChinstrap"]], 1)`) \times \text{Chinstrap} + `r round(penguins_b[["speciesGentoo"]], 1)` \times \text{Gentoo}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}

#| out-width: "100%"

) +

    y = "Body mass (g)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: {.column width="45%" .smaller}

```{.r}
lm(body_mass ~ flipper_len +
     bill_len + species,
   data = penguins)
```

```{r}
get_regression_table(penguins_model) |>
```

::::

## Penguin weights {.clr-3}

::: {.incremental .small}
- **Intercept**: An Adelie penguin with 0 mm flippers and a 0 mm bill would weigh `r round(penguins_b[["(Intercept)"]], 1)` grams (not a real penguin!)
- **Flipper length**: Controlling for bill length and species, a one-mm increase in flipper length is associated with a `r round(penguins_b[["flipper_len"]], 1)` gram increase in body mass, on average
- **Bill length**: Holding flipper length and species constant, a one-mm increase in bill length is associated with a `r round(penguins_b[["bill_len"]], 1)` gram increase in body mass, on average
- **Chinstrap**: Taking flipper and bill length into account, Chinstrap penguins weigh `r abs(round(penguins_b[["speciesChinstrap"]], 1))` grams less than Adelie penguins, on average
- **Gentoo**: Taking flipper and bill length into account, Gentoo penguins weigh `r round(penguins_b[["speciesGentoo"]], 1)` grams more than Adelie penguins, on average
:::

## House prices {.clr-3}

::: {.small}
$$
\widehat{\text{price}} = `r scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1, big.mark = "{,}")(houses_b[["(Intercept)"]])` + `r round(houses_b[["living_area"]], 2)` \times \text{living}\_\text{area} + (`r round(houses_b[["age"]], 2)`) \times \text{age} + `r scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1, big.mark = "{,}")(houses_b[["fireplaceTRUE"]])` \times \text{fireplace}
$$
:::

::::

## House prices {.clr-3}

::: {.incremental .small}
- **Intercept**: A brand new house with 0 square feet and no fireplace would cost `r scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)(houses_b[["(Intercept)"]])` (not a real house!)
- **Living area**: Controlling for age and fireplaces, a one-square-foot increase in living area is associated with a `r scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01)(houses_b[["living_area"]])` increase in price, on average
- **Age**: Holding living area and fireplaces constant, a one-year increase in a house's age is associated with a `r scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01)(abs(houses_b[["age"]]))` decrease in price, on average
- **Fireplace**: Taking living area and age into account, houses with a fireplace cost `r scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)(houses_b[["fireplaceTRUE"]])` more than houses without one, on average
:::
